summary: Design payment triggers, verification protocols, and data controls for results-based financing. Explore practical exercises and enrol in the course.
lede: Results-based financing training helps programme, finance and verification professionals link funding decisions to documented results. It covers defining indicators and payment triggers, setting evidence and sampling protocols, and applying data-quality controls to reporting workflows. Participants also practise allocating delivery and verification risks, handling disputed results, and preparing results-to-payment records for donor-funded and public-service programmes.
audienceIntro: The course is designed for professionals who connect programme delivery, results evidence, financing conditions, and payment oversight across donor-funded and public-service programmes. It is particularly relevant when your role requires you to define, verify, report, or challenge results linked to funding decisions. Donor programme managers defining results-linked disbursement conditions. Government results officers maintaining indicators and reporting evidence. Public finance specialists reviewing programme payment controls. Development consultants structuring outcome-linked programme arrangements. Independent verification providers assessing reported programme results. NGO programme leads coordinating delivery evidence and funder reporting. MEAL managers validating indicators and results data quality. Programme finance officers reconciling verified results with disbursement records. Public-service delivery managers monitoring contracted outcome commitments. Grievance officers handling complaints about results assessments or payments.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with programme results, monitoring data, or finance and delivery processes is expected. No coding or specialist software is required. You may bring an anonymized results framework or indicator for use in exercises.
